claims.text: Conventional tungsten-based refractory alloys perform well at high temperatures.
Conventional tungsten-based refractory alloys create long-lived activation products under irradiation.
Vanadium and titanium are low-activation elements suitable for replacing tungsten in a refractory HEA.
A tungsten-free refractory HEA can be designed with approximately 25 at.% each of Mo, Nb, V, and Ti.
Fusion plasma-facing components may operate at approximately 1200–1600°C under high neutron flux and plasma bombardment.
Near-equiatomic Mo, Nb, V, and Ti form a complex solid-solution HEA microstructure.
The near-equiatomic distribution of Mo, Nb, V, and Ti stabilizes the proposed complex solid solution.
Eliminating tungsten reduces the formation of long-lived activation products.
Mo, Nb, V, and Ti maintain high-temperature strength through solid-solution strengthening.
Mo, Nb, V, and Ti improve phase stability in the proposed alloy.
Solid-solution strengthening and improved phase stability maintain irradiation resistance in the proposed alloy.
The tungsten-free Mo-Nb-V-Ti HEA should exhibit lower neutron activation than conventional tungsten-based alloys.
The tungsten-free Mo-Nb-V-Ti HEA should maintain or slightly improve high-temperature mechanical performance relative to conventional tungsten-based alloys.
The tungsten-free Mo-Nb-V-Ti HEA should maintain or slightly improve irradiation resistance relative to conventional tungsten-based alloys.
Alloy processing parameters such as casting and annealing can affect the proposed material's performance.
The proposed tungsten-free HEA is suitable for use as a low-activation plasma-facing structural material in fusion reactors.
